title: Family
tagline: Family members on both sides, and how to say whose relative someone is.
canDo: You can explain who's who in your family, on both sides

grammar.title: ka, ki, ke (possessive 's)
grammar.body: X ka/ki/ke Y = X's Y. The form agrees with Y, the thing owned: ka for masculine (Nani ka ghar), ki for feminine (Ammi ki behen), ke for plural or a respected man (Ammi ke bhai). 'My' works the same: mera, meri, mere.

grammar.title: Mum's side vs dad's side
grammar.body: Maternal: Nana, Nani, Khala (+Khalu), Mamoon (+Mumani). Paternal: Dada, Dadi, Phuppo (+Phuppa), Chacha (younger, +Chachi), Taya (older, +Tai). Add 'ji' to any of them for extra respect: Khala ji, Taya ji.

grammar.title: Having = 'my X is/are'
grammar.body: Urdu has no everyday verb 'to have' for family. 'I have two brothers' is 'mere do bhai hain' (my two brothers are).

phrases.note: Also what you call any man roughly your age. The waiter is bhai. The Uber driver is bhai.
Urdu has proper terms like 'khala-zaad bhai' (khala's son), but every Pakistani family just says 'cousin'.

phrases.roman: aap ke kitne bhai behen hain?
phrases.urdu: آپ کے کتنے بھائی بہن ہیں؟
phrases.en: How many brothers and sisters do you have?
How many children do you have?

phrases.note: You will hear this sentence about Bilal more than you hear your own name.

phrases.roman: aap ki ammi ka naam kya hai?
phrases.urdu: آپ کی امی کا نام کیا ہے؟

phrases.note: The classic elder question. They're placing you on the family map.

phrases.roman: Meri Ammi Shabnam Khala ki behen hain
phrases.urdu: میری امی شبنم خالہ کی بہن ہیں
phrases.en: My mum is Shabnam Khala's sister

phrases.roman: Achha achha! Shabnam ki behen ka beta!
phrases.urdu: اچھا اچھا! شبنم کی بہن کا بیٹا!
phrases.en: Oh, of course! Shabnam's sister's son!
phrases.speaker: mrs-butt

phrases.en: How many brothers and sisters have you got?
phrases.speaker: mrs-butt

phrases.roman: Mere do bhai aur ek behen hai
phrases.urdu: میرے دو بھائی اور ایک بہن ہے
phrases.en: I've got two brothers and a sister
accept: mere do bhai aur ek behen hain

phrases.en: My cousin Bilal is a doctor!

phrases.roman: Bohat achha! Main list mein likh leti hoon
phrases.urdu: بہت اچھا! میں لسٹ میں لکھ لیتی ہوں
phrases.en: Excellent! I'll just add you to the list
phrases.speaker: mrs-butt

phrases.roman: Bilal? Doctor Bilal? Woh bhi list mein hai
phrases.urdu: بلال؟ ڈاکٹر بلال؟ وہ بھی لسٹ میں ہے
phrases.en: Bilal? DOCTOR Bilal? He's on the list too
phrases.speaker: mrs-butt

phrases.roman: Yeh meri behen ka beta hai
phrases.urdu: یہ میری بہن کا بیٹا ہے
phrases.speaker: khala

lessons.title: Ammi, Abbu & co.
lessons.blurb: Parents, siblings, kids. The people who eat your leftovers.
lessons.canDo: You can name your closest family in Urdu

teach.tip: Ammi, Ammi jaan, Mama, Mummy: families vary. Ammi is the classic.
Abbu, Abba, Papa. Same man, same opinions about the thermostat.
Brother. Also every man you need something from.
Sister. The 'h' is soft: beh-en.
Son. (Yes, and also everyone under 50, as you learned.)
Daughter. Same pattern: -a for him, -i for her.

exercises.prompt: You call the waiter at the dhaba “bhai”. Is that weird?

options.text: No. Any man around your age is bhai.
options.feedback: Correct. You now have thousands of brothers.
He is now. That's how it works.

lessons.title: Mum's side
lessons.blurb: Nana, Nani, Khala, Mamoon. The fun side (don't tell Dad).
lessons.canDo: You can name everyone on your mum's side

teach.title: Every side has its own words
teach.info: English has 'aunt' and 'uncle'. Urdu tells you exactly WHICH aunt: mum's side or dad's side, older or younger, blood or married in. Get it right and elders melt. Get it wrong and you've just called Khala 'Phuppo' (a family feud in one word).

teach.tip: Mum's dad. Nana = mum's side; remember N for 'Nani's husband'.
Mum's mum. Judge, jury, best halwa.
Mum's sister. Shabnam Khala is one of these. Brace yourself.
Khala's husband. Usually quietly watching cricket.
Mum's brother. Traditionally the one who spoils you.
Mamoon's wife. Many families say 'Mami'.

options.feedback: Phuppo is DAD's sister. Khala would like a word.
Mumani married in: she's Mamoon's wife.

exercises.prompt: Introduce Shabnam Khala to a friend.
Type the word for your mum's brother.

lessons.title: Dad's side
lessons.blurb: Dada, Dadi, Chacha, Taya, Phuppo. Older vs younger matters here.
lessons.canDo: You can name everyone on your dad's side, including older vs younger uncles

teach.tip: Dad's dad. D for Dad's side: Dada, Dadi.
Dad's mum.
Dad's OLDER brother. Seniority is everything.
Dad's YOUNGER brother. Calling Taya 'Chacha' makes him younger, and he will not thank you.
Dad's sister. In TV dramas, the villain. In real life, usually lovely. Usually.
Phuppo's husband.
Chacha's wife. (And Tai is Taya's wife.)

exercises.prompt: Your dad has an older brother. You call him…

options.feedback: Chacha is the YOUNGER brother. Taya just aged backwards and he's not happy.

exercises.prompt: Which pair are BOTH on your dad's side?
exercises.explain: D for Dad: Dada, Dadi. Then Chacha, Taya, Phuppo.

exercises.prompt: Type the word for dad's younger brother.

lessons.title: Ka, ki, ke
lessons.blurb: Mum's sister, Dad's brother: the little word that does all the work.
lessons.canDo: You can say whose relative someone is (Ammi ki behen, Abbu ke bhai)

teach.title: ka, ki, ke = 's
teach.info: Urdu says “Ammi ki behen”: Mum's sister. The little word changes to match the thing owned, not the owner: ka before a masculine word, ki before a feminine word, ke before a plural or a respected man. Behen is feminine, so: Ammi ki behen.

teach.tip: Behen is feminine → ki. And Ammi ki behen = Khala.
Same shape. Abbu ki behen = Phuppo.
An uncle is a respected man → ke. Ammi ke bhai = Mamoon.
Ghar (house) is masculine → ka.
'My' works the same way: mera (m), meri (f), mere (plural or respect).

options.feedback: bare = older. Chacha is the younger one.

exercises.prompt: Explain who Chacha is: “Dad's younger brother”

lessons.title: Meet the family
lessons.blurb: Introduce people, count siblings, answer the classic elder question.
lessons.canDo: You can introduce your family and say how many siblings you have

teach.tip: Urdu doesn't 'have' siblings: it says 'my two brothers are'.
One sister → hai (singular). Two brothers → hain.
'Bhai behen' together = siblings.
Point (discreetly) at someone at the dawat.
Elders place you by your parents. Answer with your dad's (or mum's) name: “Main Shahid ka beta hoon”.
Bara = big. Every Pakistani khandan is bohat bara.

exercises.prompt: You have two brothers. Say so.
An elder asks “Aap kis ke bete hain?” What do they want?

options.text: Your dad's name, to place you in the family
options.feedback: Exactly. Within 10 seconds they'll know your entire lineage.

lessons.title: Cousins & in-laws
lessons.blurb: Bhabhi, susral, and the cousin your parents won't stop mentioning.
lessons.canDo: You can talk about cousins and in-laws (and survive 'are you married?')

teach.tip: Just 'cousin'. Everyone code-switches here, and that's real Urdu.
Hear it once, hear it forever.
Your brother's wife. Also what you call a friend's wife.
Your spouse's family. Comes up a lot once you're married. Comes up even more before.
The question. Asked at every gathering, by every aunty.
The answer. Add 'Aunty' and a polite smile.

exercises.prompt: Rishta Aunty: “Aap shaadi-shuda hain?” You're not married yet.
Type the question every aunty asks: “Are you married?”

lessons.title: Mix it up
lessons.blurb: Mrs. Butt is approaching. Warm up for the boss.
lessons.canDo: You can use this unit's phrases without a prompt: you can explain who's who in your family, on both sides

teach.title: Mrs. Butt is approaching
teach.info: She's opened the spreadsheet. Get your Khalas and Phuppos straight before she reaches you.

exercises.setup: A wedding. Mrs. Butt has spotted someone she can't place.
exercises.question: Who is Khala introducing?

options.feedback: behen ka beta: her sister's son.
beta is son. Brother would be bhai.

exercises.prompt: Type it for the family group: “How many brothers and sisters do you have?”

boss.title: The Rishta Aunty
boss.blurb: Mrs. Butt corners you at a dawat. She has a spreadsheet. You are about to be in it.
boss.scene: A dawat at Shabnam Khala's. You're reaching for a samosa when a hand lands on your shoulder. Mrs. Butt, the neighbourhood Rishta Aunty, smiles a smile that has arranged 300 marriages.
boss.canDo: You can explain who you are in the family to a total stranger

options.reaction: You tried to say goodbye before saying hello. She has not let go of your shoulder.

m3.prompt: Place yourself in the family: your dad is Shahid, or say your mum is Shabnam Khala's sister.

options.reaction: She types 'Shahid' into her phone. Then stops. She needs more.
Her eyes light up. She KNOWS Shabnam.
'Akela!' She writes something down. It's underlined.

m8.prompt: Answer the inevitable question. Or deflect to Bilal.

options.reaction: You threw your cousin under the bus. Respect.

bye-bilal.text: Across the room, Bilal's phone buzzes. He looks up, confused. You eat your samosa in peace.

end.title: You survived the Rishta Aunty
end.text: You introduced yourself, placed yourself in the family tree, and got out alive. You are now in a spreadsheet. Everyone is. It's fine.
